title: Nine Rows of Sand
subtitle: 胡萝卜与蔬菜 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 胡萝卜与蔬菜（生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：胡萝卜与蔬菜（生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：carrot　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 carrot 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1949 my mother was sent to pull ① a carrot she could not straighten, and she said the straightening was the whole of the lesson. The ② carrot, meaning the root and not the row, was nine inches long and was pulled by whoever came last; a carrot, she said, is the only thing in a garden that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ carrot in that garden had the same sand, and the ④ carrot at the end, meaning the one the grower kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever pulled properly. A carrot, my grandmother said, is nine parts water and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the water is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ carrot was the whole of the promise, meaning the reward it stood for and not the root. The ⑥ carrot, meaning the reward and not any of that, is the only thing in an office that everybody dangles and nobody questions; a carrot, he said, is either something you pull or the only word that means both a root and a reward. She said the reward is the part they remember.

By 1965 the ⑦ carrot had become a photograph in a report, and the report had become an argument about the sand. The ⑧ carrot of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine rows and eleven years of pulling; a carrot, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ carrot I remember is the one at the end, which was stored in 1970 and is still described as the best in the county. A ⑩ carrot, my grandmother said in 1975, is the only thing that improves by being eaten; every carrot, she said, is a reward that has agreed to look like a root. She said the reward was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 胡萝卜（指那根菜本身，与整畦相对）
C. 固定搭配：pull a carrot 拔一根胡萝卜
D. n. 胡萝卜（指园子里每一根）
E. n. 胡萝卜（指末尾那一根）
F. n. 胡萝卜（抽象：它所代表的奖赏、诱饵）
G. n. 那份奖赏（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

answers.why: pull a carrot 意为“拔一根胡萝卜”，1949 年母亲被派去拔一根她弄不直的胡萝卜。
carrot 意为“胡萝卜”，指那根菜本身而不是整畦，长九英寸，由最后走的人拔起。
carrot 指园子里每一根胡萝卜，每一根都是同样的沙土。
carrot 指末尾那一根（种菜人留的那一根），是唯一有人认真拔过的。
carrot 意为“胡萝卜”，抽象指它所代表的奖赏、诱饵，父亲说 carrot 就是那份许诺的全部。
carrot 为抽象用法，指那份奖赏本身，是办公室里人人都拿它引诱、却没人质疑的东西。
carrot 意为“胡萝卜”，到 1965 年这根 carrot 成了报告里的一张照片。
carrot 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九畦和十一年的拔菜。
carrot 意为“胡萝卜”，我记得的是末尾那一根，1970 年入窖，至今仍被说成全县最好的。
carrot 为抽象总称，祖母说胡萝卜是唯一会因为被吃掉而变好的东西。
